Every marine was cool. That's what made the movie so great. Even the small roles of under 10 minutes screen time had individual, distinct personalities. Hudson had the most screentime and had great lines, but you can appreciate the other marines too. Vasquez was great as a badass and had a lot of good screentime. She clearly had some sort of relationship with Drake, who was another clear badass. He suffers a particularly grizzly death from acid when Vazquez shoots an alien in the face.

Ferro seemed like a damned competent pilot. She didn't have more than a few lines but was exuded military precision every time she was on screen. She never panicked and went right for her sidearm when she got ambushed on the dropship; unfortunately the alien had the drop on her.

And you have to love sergeant Apone. Fed up with Hudson's bullshit, but clearly a trusted and competent squad leader. Exuded a can-do, I love the marine corp attitude. Main flaw for this guy is probably his love of the corp; he got himself killed listening to useless orders from a panicking CO. If he had switched off his headset and said 'fuck it!' he probably would have lived.

New Titanfall games are coming to iOS and Android

Yeah, this is only a small blip on my radar right now. It's interesting from a news perspective, but no matter how much I love Titanfall I don't feel that makes them any more qualified to release mobile games. Whatever they do release I'll have to judge on its own merit, and is just as likely to be bad as it is good. It's a "wait and see" kind of development. Titanfall 2, however, I am hyped for.

In my mind this is a good thing and a bad thing. The risk is that they end up turning out like Destiny, in that you end up "subscribed" to a content mill that just spits out pieces of game every few months. That's the cynical view. The more cautiously optimistic view is that they're trying to expand the universe. Titanfall actually has a pretty interesting world, with space travel, interesting/unique technology, and characters at conflict. The first game did a good job of building that world, but didn't really explore it in depth because it lacked a traditional story mode. Seeing as a sequel won't be complete for some time, this could be their attempt to expand the lore of the universe to something that can draw you in like Halo or Star Wars. I think there's potential there, but it's going to all depend on execution.
